CreateProfile.name: CreateProfile
CreateProfile.documentation:
Creates a profile, a list of the roles that Roles Anywhere service is trusted to assume. You use profiles to intersect permissions with IAM managed policies.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:CreateProfile.

CreateTrustAnchor.name: CreateTrustAnchor
CreateTrustAnchor.documentation:
Creates a trust anchor to establish trust between IAM Roles Anywhere and your certificate authority (CA). You can define a trust anchor as a reference to an Private Certificate Authority (Private CA) or by uploading a CA certificate. Your Amazon Web Services workloads can authenticate with the trust anchor using certificates issued by the CA in exchange for temporary Amazon Web Services credentials.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:CreateTrustAnchor.

DeleteAttributeMapping.name: DeleteAttributeMapping
DeleteAttributeMapping.documentation: Delete an entry from the attribute mapping rules enforced by a given profile.

DisableProfile.name: DisableProfile
DisableProfile.documentation:
Disables a profile. When disabled, temporary credential requests with this profile fail.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:DisableProfile.

DisableTrustAnchor.name: DisableTrustAnchor
DisableTrustAnchor.documentation:
Disables a trust anchor. When disabled, temporary credential requests specifying this trust anchor are unauthorized.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:DisableTrustAnchor.

EnableCrl.name: EnableCrl
EnableCrl.documentation:
Enables a certificate revocation list (CRL). When enabled, certificates stored in the CRL are unauthorized to receive session credentials.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:EnableCrl.

EnableProfile.name: EnableProfile
EnableProfile.documentation:
Enables temporary credential requests for a profile.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:EnableProfile.

EnableTrustAnchor.name: EnableTrustAnchor
EnableTrustAnchor.documentation:
Enables a trust anchor. When enabled, certificates in the trust anchor chain are authorized for trust validation.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:EnableTrustAnchor.

GetSubject.name: GetSubject
GetSubject.documentation:
Gets a subject, which associates a certificate identity with authentication attempts. The subject stores auditing information such as the status of the last authentication attempt, the certificate data used in the attempt, and the last time the associated identity attempted authentication.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:GetSubject.

ImportCrl.name: ImportCrl
ImportCrl.documentation:
Imports the certificate revocation list (CRL). A CRL is a list of certificates that have been revoked by the issuing certificate Authority (CA).In order to be properly imported, a CRL must be in PEM format. IAM Roles Anywhere validates against the CRL before issuing credentials.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ImportCrl.

ListCrls.name: ListCrls
ListCrls.documentation:
Lists all certificate revocation lists (CRL) in the authenticated account and Amazon Web Services Region.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ListCrls.

ListProfiles.name: ListProfiles
ListProfiles.documentation:
Lists all profiles in the authenticated account and Amazon Web Services Region.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ListProfiles.

ListSubjects.name: ListSubjects
ListSubjects.documentation:
Lists the subjects in the authenticated account and Amazon Web Services Region.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ListSubjects.

ListTagsForResource.name: ListTagsForResource
ListTagsForResource.documentation:
Lists the tags attached to the resource.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ListTagsForResource.

ListTrustAnchors.name: ListTrustAnchors
ListTrustAnchors.documentation:
Lists the trust anchors in the authenticated account and Amazon Web Services Region.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ListTrustAnchors.

PutAttributeMapping.name: PutAttributeMapping
PutAttributeMapping.documentation: Put an entry in the attribute mapping rules that will be enforced by a given profile. A mapping specifies a certificate field and one or more specifiers that have contextual meanings.

PutNotificationSettings.name: PutNotificationSettings
PutNotificationSettings.documentation:
Attaches a list of notification settings to a trust anchor.

A notification setting includes information such as event name, threshold, status of the notification setting, and the channel to notify.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:PutNotificationSettings.

ResetNotificationSettings.name: ResetNotificationSettings
ResetNotificationSettings.documentation:
Resets the custom notification setting to IAM Roles Anywhere default setting.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:ResetNotificationSettings.

UpdateCrl.name: UpdateCrl
UpdateCrl.documentation:
Updates the certificate revocation list (CRL). A CRL is a list of certificates that have been revoked by the issuing certificate authority (CA). IAM Roles Anywhere validates against the CRL before issuing credentials.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:UpdateCrl.

UpdateProfile.name: UpdateProfile
UpdateProfile.documentation:
Updates a profile, a list of the roles that IAM Roles Anywhere service is trusted to assume. You use profiles to intersect permissions with IAM managed policies.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:UpdateProfile.

UpdateTrustAnchor.name: UpdateTrustAnchor
UpdateTrustAnchor.documentation:
Updates a trust anchor. You establish trust between IAM Roles Anywhere and your certificate authority (CA) by configuring a trust anchor. You can define a trust anchor as a reference to an Private Certificate Authority (Private CA) or by uploading a CA certificate. Your Amazon Web Services workloads can authenticate with the trust anchor using certificates issued by the CA in exchange for temporary Amazon Web Services credentials.

Required permissions: rolesanywhere:UpdateTrustAnchor.

aliasName.documentation:
An alias for the profile. When you set an alias, the response includes the alias ARN of the profile in aliasArn.

An alias name contains 1 to 256 characters. It must begin with a letter (A-Z or a-z). It can contain only letters (A-Z and a-z), numbers (0-9), underscores (_), hyphens (-), and forward slashes (/). A forward slash can appear only between two other characters, so an alias name can't end with a forward slash or contain two in a row. Alias names that begin with aws/, in any combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, are reserved. Alias names are case sensitive.

The alias name must be unique among resources of the same type in your account and Region. If another resource of the same type already has the alias, the request fails with a ValidationException. An invalid or reserved alias name also causes a ValidationException.

If you omit this parameter or specify an empty string, the resource is created without an alias.

documentation:
Identity and Access Management Roles Anywhere provides a secure way for your workloads such as servers, containers, and applications that run outside of Amazon Web Services to obtain temporary Amazon Web Services credentials. Your workloads can use the same IAM policies and roles you have for native Amazon Web Services applications to access Amazon Web Services resources. Using IAM Roles Anywhere eliminates the need to manage long-term credentials for workloads running outside of Amazon Web Services.

To use IAM Roles Anywhere, your workloads must use X.509 certificates issued by their certificate authority (CA). You register the CA with IAM Roles Anywhere as a trust anchor to establish trust between your public key infrastructure (PKI) and IAM Roles Anywhere. If you don't manage your own PKI system, you can use Private Certificate Authority to create a CA and then use that to establish trust with IAM Roles Anywhere.

This guide describes the IAM Roles Anywhere operations that you can call programmatically. For more information about IAM Roles Anywhere, see the IAM Roles Anywhere User Guide.
